second_order: pulling and playing along with April Fools tricks
theme_note: These passages make a false football story or keep its joke performance going through mock praise, reaction material, atonement, punishment, or an added trick; what varies is whether the speaker starts or extends the joke.

second_order: testing and judging April Fools claims
theme_note: These passages work out whether a football claim is an April Fool and judge whether it fooled anyone, arrived at the right time, showed effort, or went too far; the judgments range from vigilance and brief belief to dismissal and exposure.

second_order: checking whether the spare ticket is real
theme_note: The seller and replies establish whether an April 1 ticket offer is genuine: proof and a price are offered or requested while commenters imagine and condemn a trick.

second_order: settling on a United badge and starting it
theme_note: These passages turn a general wish for United art into a chosen image, pixel guide, coordinates, first placements, and a commitment to the full badge; members contribute designs, decisions, and labour.
Members propose, start, and repeatedly call people into Discord as the place for live badge coordination, while coordinates and plans remain visible on Reddit.

second_order: relocating to a smaller badge they can defend
theme_note: These passages abandon a site where LoL is too strong, delegate a new choice, and publish a left-eye anchor for a smaller design; the practice varies from diagnosing the pressure to making the replacement location usable.

second_order: bringing helpers into the badge build
theme_note: Members explain the placement rhythm and troubleshoot stale displays so newcomers and existing builders can join the same visible work.
A neighbour asks for coexistence, the builders say any move overwrites someone, and the neighbour switches from building its own Spur to destroying United's work.

second_order: automating the crest and arguing about scripts
theme_note: The founding passage asks programmers for an auto script like one used elsewhere; later slices can extend the theme with the actual making, running, acceptance, or rejection of scripts.
The founding passage has a moderator sticky the drawing effort; later moderator support or containment can extend this theme.

second_order: spotting damage and protecting agreed borders
theme_note: Members warn about attacks, challenge a familiar account over damage, accept a repair explanation, and tell builders to leave allied logos alone; what varies is whether the suspected damage is hostile, mistaken, or a boundary violation.

second_order: recruiting badge help inside football talk
theme_note: These codes show a rivals thread continuing its football work while commenters use the gathered audience to call for badge help, answer would-be helpers, repeat the image and coordinates, and receive promises of labour; the match does not cause the campaign.

second_order: pushing back on r/place taking over the sub
theme_note: The founding passage calls r/place a fad that has taken over people's subreddits; later slices can extend the theme with requests to stop, contain, or move repeated canvas talk.

second_order: showing progress and making the crest worth displaying
theme_note: Members post crest updates, show that it is nearly finished, and call for the completed work to appear in the sidebar; later completion and retrospective display can extend this practice.

second_order: defending and repairing the crest pixel by pixel
theme_note: Members choose defensive build order, answer raids, distract intruders, call for help, place their own pixels, specify repairs, celebrate holding ground, and correct small damage; the tactics vary while the shared work is keeping the crest standing.

second_order: making truces and helping canvas neighbours
theme_note: Members repair relations after border errors, claim parley, restate a CFB truce, and ask others to respect a helping neighbour; later mutual-aid and ceasefire passages can extend the practice.

second_order: arguing whether attacking other logos is fair play
theme_note: Participants admit or question attacks on other drawings, tell one another to stop griefing and protect their own, or defend attacking as the fun of the event; the practice is the room's internal contest over what counts as acceptable play.

second_order: returning to football banter after a canvas truce
theme_note: A Liverpool visitor and United members deliberately close a courteous truce exchange by resuming rivalry insults; the shared practice is marking the temporary cooperation as over without denying that it occurred.

second_order: joking about the damaged devil after the canvas closed
theme_note: Participants inspect griefed details in the final image, correct a mistaken identification, and turn the unfinished Swedish king and their own squirrel-like devil into a new comic name.
